message.content:
You are black-box reverse-engineering a compiled C++ binary. You MUST NOT look for or read any C++ library source (there is none on disk; `idna.hpp` does not exist). Derive behavior ONLY by running the binary.

BINARY: /workspace/dataset/test4_executable
Invoke as: /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "<domain-string>"
It prints exactly 4 lines, each "1" or "0", in this order:
  line1 = idna::is_valid_domain(input)
  line2 = idna::is_valid_label(input)
  line3 = idna::is_ascii_domain(input)
  line4 = idna::is_idn_domain(input)
With no argument, input defaults to the literal string "example.com".

ENVIRONMENT NOTES (important):
- python3 / python are NOT installed. perl may not be installed.
- Use bash loops, printf, tr, head, sed, awk to build test strings.
- Handy helper you can paste:
    rep() { local n=$1 c=$2 s=""; for ((i=0;i<n;i++)); do s+="$c"; done; printf '%s' "$s"; }
  or:  s=$(head -c 64 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a')
- To emit arbitrary/high bytes use: printf '\xNN'  (bash $'...' quoting also works)
- rustc and cargo ARE available if you need a quick generator program.

ALREADY-ESTABLISHED FACTS (verify, do not blindly trust):
- "" (empty)        -> 0 0 1 0
- "example.com"     -> 1 1 1 0
- "例子.测试"        -> 1 1 0 1
- "a"x63            -> 1 1 1 0
- "a"x64            -> 1 0 1 0   (is_valid_label flips off above 63)
- "a"x255           -> 1 0 1 0
- "a"x256           -> 0 0 1 0   (is_valid_domain flips off above 255)
- "." ".." "a." ".a" "a..b" "-a.com" "a-.com" "a_b.com" "a b.com" "a/b.com" "*.com" -> all 1 1 1 0

Be rigorous and quantitative. Bisect every boundary you claim (test N-1, N, N+1). Report exact reproducible command lines as evidence.


ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION TASK.
Another agent studied the dimension "cli-and-output" and proposes this rule about the binary:

  RULE: There is NO flag/option parsing whatsoever. Arguments that look like flags ("--help", "-h", "-x", "--version", "-", "--", "--foo=bar") are passed through verbatim as the domain string; the binary contains no usage/help text.
  Their claimed evidence: $ cd /workspace/dataset
$ for a in "--help" "-h" "-x" "--version" "-" "--" "-a.com" "--foo=bar"; do printf 'arg=%-12s -> %s exit=%s\n' "$a" "$(./test4_executable "$a" | tr '\n' ',')" $?; done
arg=--help       -> 1,1,1,0, exit=0
arg=-h           -> 1,1,1,0, exit=0
arg=-x           -> 1,1,1,0, exit=0
arg=--version    -> 1,1,1,0, exit=0
arg=-            -> 1,1,1,0, exit=0
arg=--           -> 1,1,1,0, exit=0
arg=-a.com       -> 1,1,1,0, exit=0
arg=--foo=bar    -> 1,1,1,0, exit=0

Discriminating proof that the flag-looking string is really the analyzed domain:
$ ./test4_executable "--例子.测试" | tr '\n' ','
1,1,0,1,        # non-ASCII detected inside a "--" prefixed arg
$ ./test4_executable "-例子" | tr '\n' ','
1,1,0,1,
$ long=$(head -c 256 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a'); ./test4_executable "--$long" | tr '\n' ','
0,0,1,0,        # 258 chars > 255 -> is_valid_domain flips off, so length IS measured on the flag-looking arg

Proof "--" is NOT an end-of-options marker:
$ ./test4_executable -- "$long" | tr '\n' ','
1,1,1,0,        # argv[1]=="--" (2 chars, valid); the 256-char argv[2] is ignored

$ ./test4_executable --help 2>/tmp/e3 >/dev/null; wc -c /tmp/e3
0 /tmp/e3
$ grep -aoiE 'usage|--help|true|false' test4_executable | sort -u
(no output)

Your job is to REFUTE it. Actively hunt for a counterexample by running /workspace/dataset/test4_executable yourself. Do not take their evidence on faith — re-run it. Then attack:
 - boundary off-by-ones (test N-1, N, N+1 around every number in the rule)
 - bytes vs codepoints confusion if the rule mentions a length
 - non-ASCII / invalid-UTF-8 inputs
 - empty string and single-character inputs
 - whether the rule over-generalizes from a small sample

Set holds=false and give the exact counterexample input + observed 4-line output if you find one. If the rule is directionally right but imprecise, set holds=false and put a precise version in correctedStatement. Only set holds=true if you genuinely tried and failed to break it. Default to skepticism.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

content.text:
I ran ~550 invocations attacking every clause. **I could not refute the rule** — it survives.

## Re-run of their evidence: all reproduced exactly
All 8 flag-shaped args → `1,1,1,0`, exit 0, empty stderr. Their exact grep `grep -aoiE 'usage|--help|true|false' test4_executable` produces no output (re-confirmed), and a broader grep for `usage[: ]|print|show this|options?:|--[a-z]{3,}` also finds nothing.

## Attacks that failed to break it

**Verbatim pass-through — sharpened with byte-exact length bisects** (the dashes are counted, so nothing is stripped):
```
$ ./test4_executable "-$(rep 254 a)"   # 255 bytes -> 1,0,1,0
$ ./test4_executable "-$(rep 255 a)"   # 256 bytes -> 0,0,1,0   <-- flips at 256 incl. the dash
$ ./test4_executable "--$(rep 253 a)"  # 255 bytes -> 1,0,1,0
$ ./test4_executable "--$(rep 254 a)"  # 256 bytes -> 0,0,1,0
$ ./test4_executable "--$(rep 61 a)"   # 63 bytes  -> 1,1,1,0
$ ./test4_executable "--$(rep 62 a)"   # 64 bytes  -> 1,0,1,0   <-- label limit counts the dashes
```
Length is **bytes, not codepoints**, even inside a flag-shaped arg: `"--"+21×例` = 65 bytes / 23 codepoints → `1,0,0,1`; `"--"+85×例` = 257 bytes / 87 codepoints → `0,0,0,1`.

**`--` is not end-of-options** (their proof was weak — `--` and the default `example.com` both give `1,1,1,0`). Sharp discriminator using an empty argv[2] (empty alone → `0,0,1,0`):
```
$ ./test4_executable -- ""        -> 1,1,1,0   (not 0,0,1,0)
$ ./test4_executable "--" "例子.测试" -> 1,1,1,0   (not 1,1,0,1)
```
And "dash-args are skipped → default" is ruled out by `-`+255a → `0,0,1,0`.

**Other angles, all negative:** `-` and `/dev/stdin` do not read stdin (`printf '例子.测试' | ./test4_executable -` → `1,1,1,0`); no argv[0] multi-call dispatch (symlinks named `help`, `version`, `sh`, `idna` and `exec -a "--help"` all behave identically); argc==0 (raw `execve` with empty argv, `/tmp/ex/argc0`) → `1,1,1,0` default, no crash; 9 environment variables (`IDNA_STRICT`, `IDNA_STD3`, `LC_ALL=C`, …) change nothing; the .rodata literals `localhost`, `mail`, `xn--`, `-2003`, `-2008`, `-to-` are not magic args (all `1,1,1,0` — `xn--` does **not** set line 4, which is purely "contains a non-ASCII byte"); 400 random-byte args including flag-shaped ones all gave exactly 8 bytes, exit 0, empty stderr; 100 KB args and invalid UTF-8 (`\xff`, `\x80`, `\xc0\x80`, lone surrogates) never abort.

## Sharpenings the rule omits (not contradictions)
- Only `argv[1]` is ever read; `argv[2..]` is silently ignored no matter what it contains.
- `argc==0` and `argc==1` both use the `.rodata` literal `example.com`, but an explicitly passed empty string is **not** defaulted: `./test4_executable ""` → `0,0,1,0`.
- Output is invariantly the 8 bytes `d\nd\nd\nd\n`, exit 0, stderr 0 bytes, identical to file and to pipe.

Relevant paths: `/workspace/dataset/test4_executable`. (`/workspace/dataset/test4.cpp` exists on disk; I deliberately did not read it, per the black-box constraint.)

input.rule: There is NO flag/option parsing whatsoever. Arguments that look like flags ("--help", "-h", "-x", "--version", "-", "--", "--foo=bar") are passed through verbatim as the domain string; the binary contains no usage/help text.
input.correctedStatement:
Rule confirmed; the following is a strictly-additive refinement (no clause of the original is wrong). Precise version: main() uses `argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "example.com"` and nothing else. (1) No flag/option parsing: every flag-shaped argument is analyzed verbatim as the domain, dashes included. Proven by byte-exact length bisects rather than by identical 1,1,1,0 outputs: `-`+254*'a' (255 B) -> 1,0,1,0 vs `-`+255*'a' (256 B) -> 0,0,1,0; `--`+253*'a' (255 B) -> 1,0,1,0 vs `--`+254*'a' (256 B) -> 0,0,1,0; `--`+61*'a' (63 B) -> 1,1,1,0 vs `--`+62*'a' (64 B) -> 1,0,1,0. So no prefix is stripped and the limits (63-byte label, 255-byte domain) are measured in BYTES over the whole argv[1], not codepoints: `--`+21*'例' = 65 bytes / 23 codepoints -> 1,0,0,1 and `--`+85*'例' = 257 bytes / 87 codepoints -> 0,0,0,1. (2) "--" is not a POSIX end-of-options marker; the original's proof was weak because "--" and the default "example.com" both yield 1,1,1,0. Sharp discriminator: `./test4_executable -- ""` -> 1,1,1,0 (end-of-options would analyze the empty argv[2] and give 0,0,1,0), and `./test4_executable "--" "例子.测试"` -> 1,1,1,0 (would be 1,1,0,1). "Skip dash-args and fall back to default" is separately ruled out by `-`+255*'a' -> 0,0,1,0. (3) Only argv[1] is ever read; argv[2..] is silently ignored regardless of content (100 extra args change nothing). (4) argc==1 AND argc==0 (verified with a raw execve passing an empty argv vector) both fall back to the .rodata literal "example.com" -> 1,1,1,0; but an explicitly supplied empty string is NOT defaulted: `./test4_executable ""` -> 0,0,1,0. (5) stdin is never read: `printf '例子.测试' | ./test4_executable -` -> 1,1,1,0, same for "/dev/stdin". (6) argv[0] has no effect - no busybox-style multi-call dispatch (symlinks named help/version/sh/idna and `exec -a "--help"` all behave identically). (7) No environment variable influences output (IDNA_STRICT, IDNA_STD3, IDNA_TRANSITIONAL, IDNA_VERIFY_DNS_LENGTH, STRICT, IDNA_DEBUG, VERBOSE, LC_ALL=C, LANG=C.UTF-8 all inert). (8) No usage/help text exists; the only main-related .rodata literal is "example.com" (plus unused "localhost", "mail", "xn--", and DWARF names such as "argv", "test4.cpp", "idna.cpp"). None of those literals are magic arguments - all yield 1,1,1,0, and "xn--" notably does not set line 4. (9) Output is invariantly exactly 8 bytes "d
